items.summary: Google Fellow Vahab Mirrokni announced results from Antigravity's /teamwork multiagent systems, which enhance human-AI collaboration to solve open problems in mathematics, chemistry, systems software, and ML engineering. The system addresses two model limitations: unpredictable generation by pairing parallel exploration with dedicated falsifiers like the Lean 4 proof checker, and attention dispersion over long tasks via context partitioning where coordinators hand off to fresh agents from clean contexts. Researchers paired with Gemini 4 models proved information theory's Courtade–Kumar conjecture in full generality using /teamwork's Long Proof pattern, formalizing it into 50 million lines of Lean code.
items.title: Google's Antigravity /teamwork Multiagent Systems Advance Science and Engineering

items.summary: QR codes have become common for business cards, cashless payments and digital links, but creating one often means dealing with slow websites cluttered by ads, sign-up walls and invasive privacy policies that even hijack your links. A new tool called Ente QR offers a simpler alternative: it is free, requires no sign-ups or usage limits, and comes from The Intelligence's Cool Tools newsletter, which emphasizes protecting user data.
items.title: A Simple, Private QR Code Creator

items.summary: Sen. Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma hired T. Lane Wilson, a senior vice president and general counsel at the Williams Companies, as his chief of staff while the latter kept his corporate title during nearly three months in office (April 13 to July 10). The arrangement drew criticism from watchdog groups for creating an obvious conflict of interest, even though Senate ethics rules may not have prohibited it. Wilson held more than $20 million in company stock and continued selling shares worth about $450,000 while serving. Armstrong introduced a pipeline permitting bill that would benefit Williams, which cleared an initial vote. Ethics experts noted the appearance-of-conflict concern remains unresolved.
items.title: Senate Aide's Pipeline Company Ties Raise Ethics Questions

items.summary: On November 13 at 4:10 p.m. UTC (Friday), Microsoft announced its consumer products services had fully recovered, while noting only sustained recovery for its Microsoft 365 enterprise services. The company stated it was monitoring the backlog of email messages accrued during the incident before considering the issue resolved, and emphasized continued observation due to the severity of impact caused by the event.
items.title: Microsoft says consumer products services recovered; still monitoring enterprise services

items.summary: A Bloomberg investigation details how U.S.-restricted Nvidia AI chips reached a large Shanghai data center. Singapore-based Aperia bought 22 Dell servers with H800 chips, which were later shipped to Shanghai and installed in Alice Huang's company. Documents show 193 servers pledged as loan collateral worth ¥485 million (~$73 million), including 52 Super Micro servers containing H100/H200 chips requiring U.S. licenses.
items.title: चीन में एलिस हुआंग की कंपनी तक कैसे पहुंचे प्रतिबंधित Nvidia चिप्स? AI डेटा सेंटर से खुला राज

items.summary: A worldwide outage of Microsoft's Outlook, Teams, and Microsoft 365 lasted over 15 hours starting November 12. Microsoft attributed it to failing servers under network pressure, not an attack—no evidence links OpenAI or Anthropic agents to the incident.
items.title: Microsoft Outage and AI Attack Speculation

items.summary: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces mounting pressure from lawmakers over the Trump administration's handling of the Nvidia scandal, which began with revelations that a Megaspeed executive accused of ties to Chinese intelligence had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Multiple Republican senators have called for both Lutnick and Huang to testify before Congress as investigations continue.
items.title: US Commerce Secretary in Spotlight Over Nvidia Scandal

items.summary: The FAA grounded all US departures for over four hours on Friday after a communications failure overloaded aging air traffic control routers, cancelling 6,600 flights and delaying 8,600. Secretary Sean Duffy reopened airspace at 8:15pm but blamed Congress for underfunding the system.
items.title: US Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Lifted After Communications Failure Chaos

items.summary: President Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless it halts a migrant caravan heading toward the US border, intensifying tensions with its largest trading partner. Illegal crossings have fallen during his second term as Mexico deployed troops and sought White House favor. Democratic electoral gains raised hopes of more lenient immigration policy, but Stephen Miller's appointment as chief of staff—despite his role in harsh enforcement measures like raids—has undermined those expectations.
items.title: Trump Threatens New Tariffs on Mexican Goods Over Migrant Caravan

items.summary: SpaceX launched its reusable Starship rocket from Texas on Friday, aiming for a historic double catch but falling short when the Super Heavy booster splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico amid unknown causes. The upper stage continued orbiting at over 26,000 km/h. SpaceX employees cheered as it sought to advance rapid reusability toward lunar and Mars missions.
items.title: SpaceX Starship Test Falls Short of Double-Catch Goal

items.summary: On Friday, the US National Weather Service (NWS) confirmed its radars were operating normally and that its radar website remained fully operational. The agency said outdated content from isolated webpages had been circulating online, but there was no actual radar outage. Previously, its website displayed reports of nationwide internet and communications problems that could have blocked access to products or shown stale information.
items.title: NWS Confirms Radars Operating Normally Amid Rumors of Outage

items.summary: An analyst argues that China's trade surplus is often misread through the lens of zero-sum competition, using Vietnam as an illustrative case. Despite widening deficits with China and other ASEAN economies, Vietnam grew 9.95% in GDP while its exports rose 24.5%. The article attributes these patterns to comparative advantage: imported machinery and components enable domestic manufacturing that generates finished-goods exports. It notes China's own import surges—storage components up 150%, integrated circuits up 56.6%—reflecting demand for intermediate products, while services trade runs a deficit of 1.23 trillion yuan in nine months. The piece concludes that trade balances alone cannot capture economic relations; supply-chain integration and investment matter equally.
items.title: China's Trade Surplus as a Misunderstood Narrative

items.summary: A global outage lasting over 24 hours knocked out Microsoft products, including Outlook and Teams, across 74 countries. Singapore's government Outlook services were fully restored by Friday night at 11pm per GovTech. Emergency services remained operational while Singpass was unaffected. Banks such as UOB and DBS, along with SingHealth, confirmed email restoration, though some replies may be delayed.
items.title: Singapore Government Outlook Services Restored After Global Microsoft Outage

items.summary: On Friday Microsoft reported that its consumer products and services had fully recovered, while Microsoft 365 enterprise services showed only partial recovery with no timeline for full restoration. A global outage of Outlook and Teams, which disrupted communications across businesses and governments after more than 24 hours, was easing but remained unresolved. The company attributed the incident to server issues rather than malicious activity or AI.
items.title: Microsoft Consumer Products Services Recover After Global Outage

items.summary: Microsoft's November 12, 2026 outage degraded its services for over 10 hours and reached at least 74 countries, with complaints peaking near 140,000. Impact concentrated in the Americas, Europe and Australia; governments like Germany's BSI and Australia activated recovery measures. China was largely unaffected because Microsoft 365 there runs on isolated domestic infrastructure via 21Vianet, while agencies migrate to alternatives by 2027 under laws like the Cybersecurity Law. Yet concentration risk persists across Alibaba Cloud, Huawei Cloud and Tencent Cloud—true sovereignty requires interoperability and exit strategies.
items.title: The Microsoft Outage China Barely Felt: A Lesson on Data Sovereignty

items.summary: A Trump administration official running U.S. export control programs sought marquee speakers for the Bureau of Industry and Security's annual conference, considering Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as an unusual option. Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler had expressed interest in inviting Huang to speak on Jan. 10 in Washington, braging about his ability to secure attendance before the then-Nvidia chief fell out of consideration.
items.title: Nvidia Crisis Sparks Scrutiny of Agency Overseeing Chip Curbs

items.summary: A significant share of the world's displays traces back to China's Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, particularly Shenzhen. From phone screens to giant city skyline displays, the entire supply chain—from display panels to LED modules—sits within a few hours' drive, enabling rapid scaling. CGTN's Wang Tianyu investigated how Shenzhen leverages this geographic advantage to serve customers worldwide.
items.title: Shenzhen Lights Up the Asia-Pacific Display Industry

items.summary: A migrant caravan of about 1,500 people—mostly Hondurans, with several dozen Nicaraguans, roughly 100 Guatemalans, plus Haitians, Venezuelans, Cubans, Ecuadorians, and one Turk—has halted in Huixtla after advancing only ~80 kilometers from the border. Activist Luis Villagrán counts it as the 24th caravan to leave Chiapas this year; Mexico's government says it is the 10th. Trump threatened to immediately double tariffs on Mexico unless migrants are stopped, warning that pressure could force President Sheinbaum to send caravans back—a fear Vanega calls 'the real terror.' Meanwhile, U.S. migration policy remains unchanged after midterms, though Texas's Republican governor Greg Abbott has fortified the border over 12 years.
items.title: Mexico's Migrant Caravan and Trump's Tariff Threat

items.summary: Li Haitao, dean of Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business, frames AI-driven cooperation in the Asia-Pacific as a “multiplication effect.” Along the Mekong River, a young Vietnamese operator uses a Chinese smart drone to deliver precision agricultural services to local farmers. In one flight, this simple technology links Chinese innovation, Vietnamese farmland and regional markets, turning broad regional-cooperation goals into tangible benefits for communities on the ground.
items.title: Li Haitao on AI Cooperation as a Multiplication Effect

items.summary: Nvidia's founder and co-founder Jensen Huang resigned Thursday amid an affair with a woman US officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence, plus reports of a second relationship. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Harvey Jones becomes the board's first chair; no succession plan exists. Investors may discount Nvidia's leadership premium, though some see AI leadership broadening to rivals like AMD and Broadcom. The resignation risks contagion across the AI funding loop just before Anthropic's IPO. Huang championed European projects in Germany and Sweden and advised President Trump on chip exports to China, whose influence may now wane.
items.title: What is next for Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang resigns?

items.summary: Comfort, a blind Nigerian pensioner who has lived in the UK since 2000 and arrived here 26 years ago, was told by the Home Office she could return to Nigeria. Under new settlement rules announced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, her path to indefinite leave to remain now extends roughly two decades until her 80s. Lawyers at Refugee and Migrant Justice sought an exception on disability grounds, but their request was refused. Nick Beales of the charity condemned the policy as cruel, noting decision-makers conflated India with Nigeria.
items.title: UK Home Office Rejects Settlement for Blind Nigerian Pensioner; Rights Groups Criticize New Rules

items.summary: The White House announced that Trump, Putin and Xi Jinping will hold a historic joint summit on the sidelines of next week's Apec summit in Shenzhen. Topics may include global nuclear weapons reduction and Iran, though Ukraine is off the agenda. The trip also includes an ASEAN summit in the Philippines. No agreement is expected to follow the talks.
items.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic trilateral meeting in Shenzhen

items.summary: Central European University (CEU), forced by Viktor Orbán's government to relocate its teaching operations from Budapest to Vienna in 2019, is signaling renewed interest in expanding its presence in the capital as a confidence vote in Hungary's democratic future. Interim president Carsten Q Schneider says no formal talks have occurred with Péter Magyar's new Tisza-led government yet, but both sides are reaching out. The university retains only administrative staff and 312 employees in Budapest; teaching remains centered in Vienna amid concerns about student mobility across the distance.
items.title: CEU Reaches Out to Hungary's New Government After Orbán Era

items.summary: Against the backdrop of Gen Z protests across Germany and Europe, DW examines whether young people face greater challenges than Baby Boomers did in the 1990s. Youth researcher Simon Schnetzer argues both generations share difficult conditions and must unite for constructive reform. The article surveys pensions, housing, education and climate change. Pension contributors per retiree fell from 3.73 in 1957 to 2.1 by 2025, projected at 1.73 by 2045, with €118 billion [$131 billion]—about 25% of the federal budget—in subsidies. Housing costs rose sharply for low-income households; rent share climbed from ~24% in 1990 to nearly 36% in 2021. Public education spending doubled since 2011, yet Germany ranks mid-tier internationally and faces a projected teacher shortfall of around 27,000 by 2035. Climate projections warn children today may face heat waves two to seven times more often than Boomers.
items.title: Do Baby Boomers Have It Better Than Gen Z? A German Data Comparison

items.summary: China has warned the United States against tightening chip export controls, saying Beijing opposes their abuse and calls allegations a technological blockade pretext. A company founded by Alice Huang reportedly obtained Nvidia H800 chips banned since 2023 via Dell servers bought through Singapore partner Aperia Cloud Services. The row intensifies US lawmaker pressure ahead of an expected Trump-Xi meeting at the Shenzhen APEC summit.
items.title: China Warns US Over Chip Curbs as Suspected Spy's Firm Got Banned Chips

items.summary: The FAA ended the longest nationwide flight ground stop since September 2001, lasting over four hours due to an overloaded legacy air traffic control communications system. More than 8,500 flights were delayed and nearly 8,000 cancelled. Officials ruled out a cyber-attack or link to Microsoft's outage.
items.title: Longest US Ground Stop Since 9/11 Lifted After Communication Outage

items.summary: The US resumed air traffic Friday after a nearly five-hour nationwide halt caused by instability in the aging FAA communications system, which forced more than 6,500 flight cancellations and about 10,000 delays. The problem began around 3:36 p.m. Eastern as new equipment overloads were integrated into outdated infrastructure; authorities ruled out sabotage or cyberattacks and called it a precautionary measure. Officials blamed decades-old technology and urged Congress for $50 billion in emergency funding to build a replacement system, which is expected to cost roughly $31.5 billion.
items.title: US Air Traffic Resumes After Nearly Five-Hour Computer-System Shutdown

items.summary: Thousands gathered for the 94th Adelaide Christmas Pageant, marking the festive season's start. Organisers estimate about 335,000 people attended as Father Christmas arrived to close proceedings. The Magic Cave attraction remains open despite David Jones entering voluntary administration and closing stores across Australia and New Zealand.
items.title: Adelaide Christmas Pageant Draws Estimated 335,000 Amid David Jones Collapse

items.summary: On the evening of 14 September, Mahli Beardman, a 21-year-old fast bowler from Dampier in Western Australia's Pilbara region, produced what is billed as the best-ever Australian ODI debut performance. Playing against England at just six runs to his name while conceding only two wickets (6/24), he also helped Australia post 8/294 versus Zimbabwe. His remarkable figures are being hailed as a cause for celebration across regional Western Australia and hoped to inspire the next generation of country cricketers.
items.title: Mahli Beardman's Record-Breaking ODI Debut Hauls Six Wickets for Australia vs Zimbabwe

items.summary: At the National Lawyers Convention of the Federalist Society in Hamilton, Canada on November 14, 2026, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sharply criticized the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the UN. He argued that a global elite uses international law to undermine US sovereignty, citing Trump's order to sink cartel boats and Maduro's capture as examples of accusations against Washington. Defending sanctions on the ICC, he called it an unelected world tribunal accountable to no one.
items.title: Rubio Attacks ICC and International Law at Federalist Society Address

items.summary: This morning briefing covers global developments as of Saturday, November 14, 2026. Türkiye and Qatar signed five agreements in Istanbul, including a mutual defense pact ratified by parliament (279-119). The US FAA lifted a nationwide flight ground stop after a telecom outage; officials called it an emergency but not necessarily a cyberattack, with over 10,000 flights delayed or canceled. Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen at the APEC summit to discuss nuclear weapons reduction. In health news, Nigeria's largest diphtheria outbreak reached 28,151 cases and 1,126 deaths; the US lost its measles elimination status with 5,400 reported cases in 2026.
items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 14, 2026

items.summary: Microsoft announced that its consumer products services had fully recovered at 4:10 p.m. UTC on Friday, November 16, 2026 (GMT). In contrast, the company reported only sustained recovery for Microsoft 365 enterprise services and stated it was monitoring a backlog of email messages accrued during the incident before considering that issue resolved. Citing the severity of the impact, Microsoft said it would continue monitoring for an extended period to ensure no additional mitigative actions were required.
items.title: Microsoft Reports Consumer Services Recovery; Enterprise Still Being Monitored

items.summary: Tesla invited select customers to place orders for the driverless two-seat Cybercab, which lacks a steering wheel and pedals, expanding from its Austin robotaxi service into limited consumer availability. Individual reservations cost $29,990 plus a required $299 monthly subscription. Tesla's AI head Ashok Elluswamy said it will operate unsupervised across the same areas as the fleet, though regulators may still intervene; an NHTSA probe opened shortly after its September debut.
items.title: Tesla Opens Cybercab Orders to Select Customers

items.summary: As President Trump prepares to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping next week, lawmakers on both sides of Congress are pressing for tighter restrictions on technology exports amid the Nvidia scandal. Analysts say the affair encapsulates U.S.-China rivalry over AI chips and national security. The strategy in Washington has been focused on controlling where California-based Nvidia's best chips go. But China hawks now have a story with a name and a face to support their argument, while Beijing warns against using the episode as a pretext for new restrictions.
items.title: The Nvidia Scandal's China Chip Fallout

items.summary: The JioBlackRock Flexi Cap Fund trimmed its holdings, selling ITC shares worth Rs 10.92 crore and exiting 17 stocks including Yes Bank (1.82 crore shares), Billionbrains Garage Ventures, CESC, REC and Hindalco Industries. It added Punjab National Bank and increased exposure across 27 stocks while holding 129 in October versus a September AUM of Rs 3,149 crore.
items.title: JioBlackRock Flexi Cap Fund Portfolio Changes in October

items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang is leaving the company, forfeiting roughly $108 million in unvested restricted stock units. This represents just 0.07% of his estimated $144.5 billion net worth, which remains overwhelmingly tied to his ~812 million Nvidia shares valued at about $135 billion—nearly 97% of his fortune and making him the company's largest individual shareholder. His departure coincides with Nvidia's market value falling below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025, though his existing holdings remain largely intact.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Exit and Remaining Wealth

items.summary: Elon Musk signed a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned amid scrutiny over alleged extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence services. The controversy drew support from President Donald Trump and Musk, who has emphasized the importance of company founders. Questions persist about Huang's personal conduct and leadership at Nvidia, where he co-founded the AI chip supplier in 1993.
items.title: Musk Endorses Move to Reinstate Huang at Nvidia

items.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told senior executives, including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld, that his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang was routine business. The two people are not related but share a surname. After press scrutiny, an independent probe by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz launched. Beijing denies she is a spy; Reuters has not verified it. Huang resigned as CEO Thursday and apologized for being unfaithful without naming Alice Huang. Nvidia's stock fell more than 30% from its October 6 high, wiping out over $1.8 trillion in market capitalisation.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang misled executives over affair with Alice Huang; resigns amid scandal

items.summary: Microsoft reported that its consumer products services had fully recovered at 4:10 p.m. UTC on Friday, while Microsoft 365 enterprise services were still experiencing sustained recovery. The company said it was monitoring the backlog of email messages accrued during the event and noted that, due to the severity of the incident's impact, it would continue monitoring for an extended period to ensure no additional mitigative actions are required.
items.title: Microsoft Restores Consumer Services After Outage

items.summary: Microsoft apologised after a global outage disrupted Teams, Outlook and Copilot AI for nearly a day across more than 70 countries. The company ruled out a cyberattack, attributing the disruption to a technical fault from an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a later change. Services were restored gradually amid airline and business disruptions in India.
items.title: Microsoft Apologises for Global Outage, Rules Out Cyberattack

items.summary: Elon Musk endorsed a petition seeking the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, commenting days after Huang's reported resignation amid allegations involving his personal relationships. His support joins backing from figures including President Donald Trump. The controversy centers on reports that Huang had extramarital relationships with Kimberly Powell and Alice Huang, raising national security concerns given her suspected ties to Chinese intelligence services.
items.title: Elon Musk Backs Petition to Reinstate Jensen Huang at Nvidia

items.summary: Nvidia's board has approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor to Jensen Huang, who resigned amid scrutiny over alleged extramarital relationships. The Financial Times reported the move following his departure after 33 years at the helm. Nvidia says succession is still in early stages and calls candidate speculation premature; CFO Colette Kress serves as interim CEO while employees back a petition for Huang's return.
items.title: Who Could Replace Jensen Huang At Nvidia? Arm CEO Rene Haas Emerges As Potential Successor

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit 2026, said the US-India trade deal is expected to close soon. He noted that most issues are sorted and remaining concerns lie more on the American side than New Delhi's, with hopes of concluding it shortly. Negotiators typically withhold such details during talks.
items.title: Jaishankar on India-US Trade Deal Progress at HT Leadership Summit 2026

items.summary: On the second day of Chhath Puja, BJP leader Pradeep Bhandari criticized Congress's Rahul Gandhi over remarks from last year's festival. Sharing a one-year-old clip in which Gandhi called "Chhath Puja" a drama, Bhandari demanded a public apology and accused him of disrespecting Hindu sentiments and the people of Bihar. The attack followed Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray accusing BJP of using Chhath Puja reels to sow discord in Maharashtra.
items.title: 'Chhath Puja not drama': BJP rakes up year-old video to target Rahul Gandhi

items.summary: On Jawaharlal Nehru's 137th birth anniversary—also Children's Day in India (s0)—PM Narendra Modi paid tribute via X, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh recalled his role in the freedom struggle and early independent-India leadership, and opposition leader Rahul Gandhi called him 'jewel of India,' emphasizing Swaraj as citizens' participation. Nehru was born November 14, 1889, died May 27, 1964 (s10), became first PM August 15, 1947 (s11). Schools and government bodies hold commemorative events; the UN declared Universal Children's Day on November 20 in 1954, while India marked his birthday as National Children's Day from 1964 onward (s8-s16).
items.title: 'Jewel of India': PM Modi, Rahul Gandhi, Rajnath Singh pay tributes to Nehru on birth anniversary

items.summary: As of October 31, 2026, nine equity mutual funds surpassed Rs 70,000 crore in assets under management (AUM), with the top four each exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore. Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund led at Rs 1.46 lakh crore; HDFC's three funds ranged from Rs 1.10 to Rs 1.00 lakh crore, followed by SBI Aggressive Hybrid (Rs 85,922 crore), Nippon India Small Cap (Rs 76,902 crore), ICICI Pru Large Cap (Rs 76,895 crore), Kotak Arbitrage (Rs 76,415 crore) and ICICI Pru Balanced Advantage (Rs 71,892 crore).
items.title: Nine Equity Mutual Funds Cross Rs 70,000 Crore AUM as of October 31, 2026

items.summary: A preliminary probe into the November 11 derailment of the Kolkata-Sairang Express near Guwahati points to a malfunctioning main braking system, with questions raised over whether crew conducted mandatory brake feel and power tests. Officials suggest station staff isolated the brake pipe angle cock under an outdated locomotive-change procedure after electrification ended that practice. The Railway Board has directed all zonal railways to conduct these two tests post-handover and ordered a safety drive from November 12-18, with discrepancies reported by November 20.
items.title: Kolkata-Sairang Express Derailment Probe Points to Brake Failure and Missed Safety Checks

items.summary: Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi arrived in Hyderabad ahead of the Bharat Summit, participating in a large bike rally with gig workers and riding pillion on one worker's scooter. Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy also joined the event. Separately, BJP and Congress leaders are exchanging allegations over central-government phone tapping.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Joins Gig-Worker Bike Rally in Hyderabad Ahead of Bharat Summit

items.summary: Political tensions have intensified between the BJP and Congress after Rahul Gandhi accused the central government of phone tapping, alleging foreign influence. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi questioned Gandhi's credibility while defending PM Modi's use of teleprompters. Opposition leaders backed Gandhi by recalling past surveillance incidents like Pegasus.
items.title: BJP and Congress Clash Over Rahul Gandhi's Phone Tapping Claims Amid Rising Political Tensions

items.summary: Helle Lyng Svendsen, a Norwegian journalist known for confronting Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his 2025 visit to Norway, alleges the Indian embassy in Oslo revoked her visa moments before she was set to depart for Hyderabad. She had been scheduled as a delegate at the Congress government's Bharat Summit in Telangana. In an interview with Dagsavisen, Svendsen blames Home Minister Amit Shah and claims officials told her the cancellation came 'on orders from above.'
items.title: Norwegian Journalist Blames Home Minister for Visa Cancellation Ahead of Bharat Summit

items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari asked 12,000 people who allegedly received Banglar Bari housing funds fraudulently under the previous TMC government to refund them by November 30. Verification reportedly found 57,000 ineligible beneficiaries delisted; around 12,000 had already been paid ₹60,000 each in a second instalment disbursed alongside one million others, totaling ₹10,323 crore to roughly 17.21 lakh eligible recipients.
items.title: West Bengal CM demands refunds from fraudulently aided housing beneficiaries amid scheme probe

items.summary: Brett Easton Ellis’s 1991 novel American Psycho follows Patrick Bateman, an investment banker in 1980s New York City obsessed with appearances while secretly committing murders. Mary Harron’s 2000 film largely replaces the graphic violence with comedy of manners about Wall Street elites, leaving open whether Bateman is a real killer or fantasist.
items.title: American Psycho and the Art of Depicting a Monster

items.summary: Buying a home in India requires an upfront down payment of roughly 10-25% after banks finance up to 90% under RBI LTV rules. Rising prices—up 59% across top seven cities from Rs 5,826 to Rs 9,260 per square foot (2021-2025)—have squeezed buyers. Experts caution against overpaying or draining emergency savings.
items.title: How Much Down Payment Should You Make on a Home?

items.summary: A Madras High Court bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi ruled on November 12 that a community's inclusion in the Other Backward Classes (OBC) list cannot be treated as permanent or automatically justified merely because it has enjoyed reservation benefits for decades. The court said the Tamil Nadu government must demonstrate, to its satisfaction, the constitutional validity of any challenged inclusion or continued retention whenever someone contests classification. Admitting a petition by G Kodeeswaran challenging provisions in the 2016 Government Servants Act granting Backward Class and Most Backward Class status to several Christian communities and converts, the bench found serious doubts over absent objective data on social and educational backwardness and ignored expert commission recommendations. The petitioner argued conversion could grant OBC benefits even to a Brahmin joining the Church of South India, prompting the court to order a serious re-examination of Tamil Nadu's reservation framework.
items.title: Madras High Court Rules OBC Reservation Inclusion Not Permanent or Self-Justifying

items.summary: Nearly two months after a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped at knifepoint in Delhi's Astha Kunj Park on her September 22 birthday, police filed a 450-page chargesheet against three accused—Asif, Hemant and Mukesh—at Saket Court. The survivor alleges she was assaulted twice with weapons while her friend was held; the third man is referred to as Deepu.
items.title: Delhi Gang Rape Chargesheet Filed Against Three Accused

items.summary: On November 14, teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest captain in men's T20 history at 15 years and 232 days. Leading Bihar to open the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) 2026-27 against Saurashtra at Holkar Stadium, Indore, he had won the toss and elected to bat first. The Bihar Cricket Association named a 17-member squad with Sooryavanshi captain for two matches; Suraj Kashyap was his deputy. He previously served as vice-captain of East Zone under Ishan Kishan in the Duleep Trophy, briefly leading when Kishan left due to injury.
items.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Becomes Youngest Men's T20 Captain at 15

items.summary: Delhi Police allege a serving Indian Air Force wing commander traded classified military information to a Pakistani intelligence-linked operative in exchange for nude photographs, helping install spyware on five subordinates' devices. Contact ran 21 days (Jan 12–Apr 1, 2026). WhatsApp data shows 3,008 messages and 65 photos exchanged. Leaked details covered a secret drone unit, fighter deployments in Leh, and exercises at Mahajan Field Firing Range.
items.title: IAF Wing Commander Allegedly Traded War Plans for Nudes; Devices Spywared
